JMFC, MACT, GOWRIBIDANUR, DISMISSING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
The appeal is filed by the claimant being aggrieved by dismissal of the claim petition and seeking for compensation.

2. It is the case of the claimant that on 02.12.2009 at about 5.00 p.m., the claimant was riding the motor cycle carrying the daughter of one Srinivasa by name Kum.Aruna from her school to Dhandiganahalli as pillion rider and the said motor cycle was hit by another motor cycle, due to which, the claimant and the pillion rider Kum.Aruna were fallen down and sustained injuries and then the claim petition filed by the claimant was dismissed on the reason of suspicious accident.
Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant submitted that just because there is a delay in lodging the compliant cannot be a ground to reject the claim petition.
It is submitted that soon after the accident, the claimant and the daughter of Srinivasa by name Kum.Aruna have been admitted to the hospital.
There is hospital records mentioning that the claimant and Kum. Aruna have been admitted with the history of road traffic accident.
Therefore, the medical records prove that the claimant has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident, which is not rightly considered by the Tribunal.
Hence, prays to allow the appeal and grant compensation.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent - Insurance Company justified the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
5. In the present case, it is the case of the claimant that the claimant and Kum. Aruna have sustained NC: 2024:KHC:20958 injuries in the motor vehicle accident on 02.12.2009 at 5.00 p.m.
The claimant has produced the medical documents and evidence of CSI Hospital, Chickballapura.

The Sri. Ramakrishna vs The Manager on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135867711/
2 Tribunal assigned the reason that there is no mentioning about the case sheet that the claimant and Kum. Aruna have been admitted in the Government Hospital.

sentences.text:
It is the case of the claimant that initially the claimant and Kum. Aruna were admitted to the Government Hospital, Chickballapura,
but the case sheet of Government Hospital, Chickballapura has not been produced by the claimant.
Further, there is delay in lodging the complaint and there is no any damage found on the bike.
On these reasons, the Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition.

6. It is case of the claimant that immediately after the accident, the claimant and Kum. Aruna admitted to the Government Hospital, Chickballapura, but the case sheet was not produced and just because there is a delay in NC: 2024:KHC:20958 lodging the complaint cannot be a sole ground to dismiss the claim petition as per the principles of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of RAVI VS. BADRINARAYAN AND OTHERS reported in CIVIL APPEAL NO. 1926 OF 2011.

entities.text: RAVI VS. BADRINARAYAN AND OTHERS reported in CIVIL APPEAL NO. 1926 OF 2011
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The delay in lodging the complaint can be considered on the facts and circumstances of each case whether the factual injuries are occurred or not?
Therefore, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, the case is remanded to the Tribunal for fresh consideration in accordance with law.

Therefore, the judgment and decree passed by the Tribunal is set aside and accordingly,
remanded.
Further observations are made above are only submissions of the learned counsel for the claimant/appellant and shall not be construed as discussion on the merits of the case.
Hence, the Tribunal is directed to consider the case in accordance with law.

7. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:20958 ORDER 1) The appeal is allowed.
2) The judgment and decree dated 22.06.2017 passed in MVC.No.50/2011 by the Court of the Senior Civil Judge and JMFC/MACT at Gowribidanur is set aside.
3) The matter is remanded to the Tribunal for fresh consideration in accordance with law.
4) All the contentions are left open.
5) The parties are given liberty to adduce any further evidence if so are desired.
6) The parties shall appear before the Tribunal on 15.07.2024.
7) The parties shall appear before the Tribunal without expecting any notice from the Tribunal.
8) The Tribunal is directed to dispose of the petition within nine months from 15.07.2024.
